title: Finite-fibre affine refinement of a locally quasi-finite etale-source composite
statement: Let $W,Z$ be affine schemes and $X$ any scheme [def-pc-scheme]. Let $q:X\to W$ be etale [def-weil-etale-morphism] and surjective on underlying points, and let $h:W\to Z$ be a morphism such that $h\circ q$ is locally quasi-finite [pqf-def-quasifinite]. There exist an integer $m\geq0$ and affine open subschemes $A_1,\ldots,A_m\subseteq X$ such that $W=\bigcup_{j=1}^m q(A_j)$ and each restricted composite $h\circ(q|_{A_j}):A_j\to Z$ is quasi-finite and has finite fibres [pqf-def-quasifinite]. Moreover, for every $z\in Z$, $h^{-1}(\{z\})=\bigcup_{j=1}^m q(\{a\in A_j:h(q(a))=z\})$ as subsets of $W$, and $h^{-1}(\{z\})$ is finite. There is no quasi-compactness assumption on $X$ or $q$, no separation assumption and no Noetherian assumption. The integer $m$ may be zero when $W$ is empty.

source.place: Tag 03X4 (lemma-locally-quasi-finite-etale-local-source), finite-fibres paragraph, expanded to arbitrary etale source using Topologies Tag 0218 (lemma-etale-affine) and Morphisms Tags 01TH, 01SH, 01S7, 01TJ, 02NH.

proof.text: Cover $X$ by its affine open subschemes $A$ using [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis]. Since $q$ is an open map by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-morphism-open-map], every $q(A)$ is open in $W$. Surjectivity of $q$ implies these images cover $W$. The affine scheme $W$ is quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs], so the definition of quasi-compactness selects finitely many of these images covering $W$. Denote the corresponding affine opens by $A_1,\ldots,A_m$. If $W$ is empty, take the empty family.

source.place: Tag 0218 (lemma-etale-affine), supplying the omitted proof for a singleton covering by affine opens and finite subcover selection.

proof.text: For each selected $A_j$, restrict the locally quasi-finite morphism $h\circ q:X\to Z$ to the source open $A_j$ and the target open $Z$ itself. By [lem-weil-pbc-lqf-restriction-to-opens], $f_j=h\circ(q|_{A_j}):A_j\to Z$ is locally quasi-finite. Its source and target are affine, so [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-affine-schemes-affine] makes $f_j$ affine, and clause (3) of [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence] makes it quasi-compact. Now [pqf-lem-qf-locqf-qc] gives that $f_j$ is quasi-finite. By the forward implication of [pqf-lem-qf-finitefibres], $f_j^{-1}(\{z\})$ is finite for every $z\in Z$.

Fix $z\in Z$. If $a\in A_j$ satisfies $h(q(a))=z$, then $q(a)\in h^{-1}(\{z\})$. Conversely, if $w\in h^{-1}(\{z\})$, the image cover from step 1 gives $j$ and $a\in A_j$ with $q(a)=w$; then $h(q(a))=h(w)=z$. This proves the stated equality of subsets. Each term on its right is the image under $q$ of the finite set $f_j^{-1}(\{z\})$ from step 2, hence finite. A union of finitely many finite sets is finite. For $m=0$ the equality is between empty sets. This proves every asserted fibre statement without any quasi-compactness assumption on $X$ or $q$.
